title: Apply for a permit to acquire a firearm (PTA)
summary: This page explains how to apply for a permit to acquire a firearm (PTA) if you already hold a current NSW firearms licence or permit.
intro:
To acquire a firearm, you must be the holder of a current NSW firearms licence or permit. You're then able to apply for a permit to acquire a firearm (PTA).

The category of licence or permit you hold will indicate what category of firearm you're eligible to possess. For example, if you hold a category B licence or permit, you're only authorised to acquire a category B firearm.

Note: If any personal or business details have changed you must update them before you apply for your PTA.To do so, visit either:
who_can_apply: You must hold a current NSW firearms licence or permit.
You may only apply for the type of firearm that your category of licence authorises you to possess.
Probationary pistol licence (PPL) holders can only apply for a PTA in the second 6 months of their pistol licence.
what_you_need: Proof of identity documents (such as your driver licence and birth certificate).
Your current firearm licence or permit number.
A current credit card (Visa or Mastercard) for payment (if applicable).
A Pistol Firearms Safety Training (PPL) Completion Certificate – PDF (for probationary pistol licence holders only).
A COPS Event Number to confirm adequate safe storage, unless you are storing your firearms at your club.
Club confirmation (this is triggered automatically when providing your nominated club details in the online PTA application).
If applying for a handgun for sports target shooting, you also need the required documentation.

how_to_steps.text: You will be taken to the NSW Police Force Community Self Service Portal.
Check that you have all the documentation required.
Follow the prompts to complete your application.

more_info.text: If you have any questions relating to firearms licences, please call the Firearms Registry customer service line on 1300 362 562, between 9am and 4pm Monday to Friday (excluding public holidays).

faqs.q: Who can apply for a Permit to Acquire a Firearm (PTA)?
faqs.a: You must hold a current NSW firearms licence or permit. The category of your licence or permit determines what category of firearm you are eligible to possess.

faqs.q: What do I need if I am a probationary pistol licence (PPL) holder?
faqs.a: PPL holders can only apply for a PTA in the second 6 months of their pistol licence. You can check your PPL issue date on the Firearms Registry Public Register.

faqs.q: What documentation do I need to apply for a PTA?
faqs.a: You need proof of identity (like a driver licence and birth certificate), a MyServiceNSW Account, your current firearm licence or permit number, and a current credit card for payment (if applicable).
